about: The Orthogonal technology table for one job, light at night, and what it needs. Read by orthogonal/grow.js (CAF after Hordijk 2023, the keep rule after Arthur and Polak 2006); the same table grows every world, and only the endowment changes. A row's jobs are what it makes; inputs are consumed, every one needed; tools are catalysts, any one enough. Each Earth row is the version that came into general use, as the ledger records light in use (the sources of the brief's ledger are Fouquet and Pearson's), with what that version needed; its date is that version's, and its source is one opened for this table, or the gap is declared. A row with no date is invented for a world, and says so. Written 2026-11-21 by the engine's builder; read row by row before commit. Known misses: Mediterranean vegetable-oil lamps, al-Razi's kerosene (9th century), coke iron, the Welsbach mantle and the carbide lamp are not in the table; no row has a quantity or a price.

ties.why: Coal gas and wood gas are one structure (a fuel heated in a cast-iron retort, known from gas chemistry), so the rule cannot choose between them; the table lists coal gas first because Earth took it.
ties.source: Nordhaus (1996), in Bresnahan and Gordon (eds.), The Economics of New Goods, University of Chicago Press, section 1.2.6: town gas was produced from coal; and Fortier-Dubois, Historical Tech Tree (2025), 'Public gas lighting' takes coal gas as its component and wood gas as an inspiration

rows.label: Fungi farmed on logs, for food
Foxfire: wood that glows where fungi rot it
This world's luminous fungi, farmed on wood
rows.invented: Invented for the world where the fungi came early: its lignin-eating fungi, the land's decomposers for longer, include strains that glow bright enough to read by, and they are grown on wood as a crop. Earth's glowing fungi are far dimmer (foxfire).

rows.label: A luminous culture kept wet under glass
rows.invented: Invented: a culture of the bright strains on a wooden spindle, kept wet and breathing inside a glass vessel.

rows.label: Mycelial street lamps
rows.invented: Invented: the culture under glass on a ceramic plinth, set along a street as its light at night.
